implementations.name: moq-rs
implementations.notes: Draft-18 line = merged draft-18-dev (PR #193) at commit a6ed4e9 (2026-07-24); drafts 14/16/18 each pin a different commit (see Dockerfile). Relay writes JSON-SEQ qlog/mlog per connection via --qlog-dir/--mlog-dir (qlogs/ volume); pub/sub rely on the relay's server-side qlog. moq-rs honors SSLKEYLOGFILE (real NSS key-log lines observed in run_20260818_181221), so captured pcaps are decryptable. Large-file relay delivery is broken at this pin (B25, deferred).

implementations.name: moxygen
implementations.notes: Builds on Meta's mvfst QUIC stack; supports WebTransport. Client image is a source build (docker/moxygen/Dockerfile.media) at the pinned commit — official images only ship moqrelayserver / moq_interop_client, so the FLV media clients (moqflvstreamerclient / moqflvreceiverclient) must be built from source. Media is FLV (h264/AAC-LC) via MoQMI, so moxygen runs use .flv files and byte comparison is approximate (transmux), not byte-exact. Draft claims are UNVERIFIED (evidence 'boot'): the WebTransport ClientHello ALPN is 'h3' and the raw moqt:// client never offers moqt-18 at this pin (B46), so no passively-observable wire artifact encodes the negotiated draft — do not trust run labels named d18 to mean draft 18.

implementations.name: imquic
implementations.notes: Picoquic-based; supports drafts 16/17/18/19 natively. Draft selection is RUNTIME via -M/--moq-draft-version (default any = offer all four ALPNs moqt-19,moqt-18,moqt-17,moqt-16 and negotiate the highest common), NOT a build-time configure flag (B4: the Dockerfile DRAFT arg is unused; the four image tags are identical). The SUB entrypoint passes '-M {draft}' so each run pins the draft its plan declares (with default 'any' the sub silently negotiates moqt-19 even on a draft-18 row, B4); the runner supplies {draft} from the run config. The RELAY entrypoint is deliberately UNPINNED: pinning the relay to '-M 18' changed its advertised WebTransport protocol to moqt-18 only and imquic-moq-relay then REJECTS moq-rs clients with 'Unsupported WebTransport protocol(s)' (close 271), whereas the default 'any' relay accepts each peer per-connection (moq-rs pub at moqt-18, imquic sub at its claimed draft), so cross-impl interop requires the unpinned relay (finding 2026-09-05). Registered as relay + pub + sub: imquic's demo moq-pub is a test-data clock generator (one timestamp object/sec, per moq-pub.c main loop) and CANNOT ingest a media file, so it is excluded from media-delivery tests but IS used by same- impl clock plans (testplans/imquic-self.yaml) where negotiation and object delivery (not file integrity) are the assertions. The PUB entrypoint also passes '-M {draft}' so an all-imquic run sees both connections negotiate the plan's claimed draft (relay.log evidence); with the default 'any' the pub silently negotiates moqt-19 on every row. That is a feature gap in its demo tool, NOT a protocol incompatibility with other implementations' pubs (interop is demonstrated per-role). RTT measurement: all three entrypoints pass '-Q /qlogs -l quic', which arms picoquic's native qlog (per-connection <cid>.server.qlog/.client.qlog; trace title 'picoquic'). Its 'recovery'/'metrics_updated' events carry smoothed_rtt/min_rtt/latest_rtt in MICROSECONDS (vs moq-rs/quinn qlogs in seconds); the runner's metrics parser auto-detects by the 'picoquic' marker. '-s /keys/sslkeys.log' additionally makes picoquic write its SSLKEYLOGFILE (each container shares the bind-mounted /keys), so capture plans can also derive wire-level RTT from decrypted QUIC ACK frames (runner already exports SSLKEYLOGFILE, but the env var alone is NOT enough: imquic only calls picoquic_set_key_log_file when -s is given). The sub entrypoint replaces the old positional-URL form (imquic is flags-only; positional args caused '[FATAL] Invalid QUIC server address'); -n is namespace, -N is track name. '-t hex' is REQUIRED: imquic's payload reaches stdout only via IMQUIC_LOG (g_print) when a payload type is set, and its target_file option is not wired to any CLI flag. 'text' mode uses printf('%.*s') and truncates at the first NUL byte, which drops MP4 payloads (box sizes start with 0x00); 'hex' (%02x per byte) is lossless. Without -t the artifact is only 'Incoming object:' metadata (see B18/B2).

implementations.name: lldash-h2

entrypoints.relay: sh -c "echo relay started; exec nginx -g 'daemon off;'"
entrypoints.pub: sh -c 'echo lldash-h2 pub ready; cat {file} > /dev/null; echo pub_started; sleep 1'

implementations.notes: LL-DASH baseline over HTTP/2 (TCP+TLS). decisions.md D8 H2 = TCP HOL baseline. Origin nginx:alpine http2 443 with certs from harness/certs.py; client httpx[http2] fetches MPD+segments sequentially (2s segment = 2s MoQ group, decisions.md D2.2). Port 443 to mirror MoQ TLS. Mounts /data for MPD/segments + /certs for TLS. TTFO measured via client time_to_first_chunk_ms log.

implementations.name: lldash-h3

entrypoints.relay: sh -c "echo relay started; exec caddy run --config /etc/caddy/Caddyfile --adapter caddyfile"
entrypoints.pub: sh -c 'echo lldash-h3 pub ready; cat {file} > /dev/null; echo pub_started; sleep 1'

implementations.notes: LL-DASH baseline over HTTP/3 (QUIC+TLS). decisions.md D8 H3 = QUIC baseline isolates app semantics (both QUIC). Origin caddy:alpine h3 443/udp with same certs + SSLKEYLOGFILE for Wireshark decrypt; client aioquic/httpx fallback. Same 2s segment alignment. Together H2+H3 show transport vs object-model win vs MoQ.
